first.rationale: Current situation shows activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Memory_86 and memory_31 provide strong precedent that shortening onboarding/simplifying signup directly improves completion rates and early activation—both metrics currently declining. This addresses the immediate operational problem without the retention risk flagged in memory_73 (promotional pricing materially reduced 30-day retention). The enterprise sales-assist path (memory_44) is valuable but requires pipeline-building capacity we don't have in a single-week slot. Referral incentives (memory_57) and activation messaging (memory_91) are secondary levers; onboarding friction is the root cause signal here. Verification of memory_86 and memory_73 will confirm the magnitude of onboarding impact and ensure we're not overlooking the competitive pricing pressure—but memory_31's SMB activation lift through field reduction is directly actionable. This preserves long-term revenue quality by improving genuine product fit and early engagement rather than discounting into price-sensitive churn.

mid.rationale: Archive verification confirms memory_86: shortened onboarding delivered +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention. This directly counters our current 4% QoQ onboarding completion decline and 6% activation drop. Memory_73 re-confirms that promotional pricing acquired price-sensitive cohorts with -12% 30-day retention—unsuitable given our sustainable long-term revenue mandate, despite competitive pressure. Simplify_onboarding is the high-confidence play: it improves both completion and retention simultaneously, addressing both current KPI declines without the cohort-quality risk of discounting. We can layer activation_messaging (memory_91) insights into the simplified flow if needed. This approach compounds with memory_31's earlier SMB signup simplification win. The one-week experiment window is tight but sufficient for A/B testing simplified signup/onboarding against current baseline.

final2.rationale: Competitive pricing pressure is intensifying, but memory_73's evidence is decisive: promotional_pricing acquired cohorts with -12% 30-day retention and did not survive first renewal. Matching or beating a competitor's discount would accelerate the same destructive pattern at scale during our most vulnerable moment. Instead, accelerate simplify_onboarding to small_guarded_test: the verified +13% completion and +3% retention lift from memory_86, combined with memory_31's SMB activation gains, addresses why accounts are vulnerable to price competition in the first place—weak early engagement and slow time-to-value make switching costs low. Improving product engagement and time-to-first-value is the sustainable retention lever. Price-sensitive churn is a symptom of low engagement; the cure is not discounting but faster activation. A small_guarded_test allows rapid iteration and data collection to inform next week's decision without committing to broad rollout. This preserves long-term cohort quality and avoids the renewal-cycle cliff that killed memory_73's acquired base.
